adult-blood-volume: Your own body: a blood donation is half a litre and barely dents it; picture a few big drink bottles.
adult-bones: Count the bones in one hand (about 27), times four for hands and feet, then add ribs, spine and skull.
tallest-person: Your own height and a 2 m doorway: the tallest basketball players are about 2.3 m, and the record beats them.
elephant-pregnancy: A human's is 9 months and a horse's about 11; the biggest land animal takes longer still.
eiffel-tower-height: Count it in storeys: about 100 floors of 3 m, two or three times a big office tower.
new-york-city-population: The US has 340 million people and New York is its biggest city; London has about 9 million.
iss-orbit-time: Earth is about 40,000 km round (a little more up there); at 27,600 km/h that's about an hour and a half.
moonwalkers: Apollo 11 to 17, less the failed 13, is six landings, with two astronauts walking on each.
neapolitan-pizza-oven: A home oven tops out near 250 °C; a wood-fired oven that bakes a pizza in 90 seconds is about twice that.
a380-capacity: A normal airliner seats about 180; the A380 has two full decks the length of a jumbo: four or five times that.
olympic-pool-volume: It's 50 m by 25 m and about 2 m deep: 2,500 cubic metres of a thousand litres each.
marathon-distance: A fit runner does about 10 km an hour, and a marathon takes them about four hours.
longest-tennis-match: A long five-set match lasts four or five hours; the record is a few of those back to back.
piano-keys: Picture the keyboard: seven octaves of 12 keys, plus a few at the ends.
czech-beer: A pint a day is about 200 litres a year; spread it over everyone, children included, and it halves.
breath-hold-record: You can hold yours for about a minute; trained divers manage many times that.
ostrich-egg-weight: A hen's egg is about 60 g, and an ostrich egg holds about two dozen of them.
hummingbird-heart-rate: Your heart beats about 70 a minute; small animals' hearts race, and a hummingbird is tiny: many times faster.
cheetah-top-speed: As fast as a car on a main road, and over twice Usain Bolt's top speed.
antarctica-winter-population: About 30 countries keep a few bases each, with a few dozen people wintering at each.
hot-dog-eating-record: You might manage a hot dog a minute, 10 in 10 minutes; champions are several times faster.
earth-spin-speed: Earth's 40,000 km circumference goes round once in 24 hours.
bolt-top-speed: 100 m in 9.58 s is about 10.4 m/s, 37.6 km/h on average, and his top speed is a bit more.
high-jump-record: A tall jumper is about 1.95 m and clears a bar well above his own head.
moon-visible-share: It always shows us one face, so about half, plus a little more from its wobble.
wright-first-flight-year: Planes fought in the First World War, so the first flight came a decade or more before 1914.
first-youtube-video-year: Your own life: YouTube was there before smartphones, when videos played on a laptop.
fingernail-growth: You trim your nails every week or two, about a millimetre each time.
oldest-person-age: People reaching 100 make the local news; the record is a couple of decades past that.
lunar-day: It shows us the same face, so it turns once per orbit: a day there is a month here.
perseverance-trip: Trips to Mars take months, not days or years, and launch when the planets line up.
longest-space-stay: Space station crews usually stay about six months; the record is a good deal longer.
hen-eggs-per-year: A laying hen gives about an egg a day, with some days off.
elephant-daily-food: You eat about 2 kg a day at 70 kg; an elephant weighs 5 or 6 tonnes and eats plants, which give less.
oldest-bread: Farming began some 10,000 to 12,000 years ago, and bread is at least as old as farming.
us-penny-cost: The Mint stopped making pennies because each one cost more than a cent to make: a few cents.
concorde-speed: An airliner cruises at about 900 km/h, and Concorde crossed the Atlantic in about half the time.
football-pitch-length: Stride it out, or picture a running track's 100 m straight.
tour-de-france-distance: 21 stages over three weeks, at about 170 km a day.
f1-fastest-pit-stop: On TV a pit stop is over in a blink, a couple of seconds.
record-transfer-fee: Big transfers run to about 100 million euros; the record is about twice that.
people-ever-born: 8 billion alive now, and hundreds of millions at a time for thousands of years before, with short lives: over 100 billion.
first-homo-sapiens: Farming began about 12,000 years ago and cave paintings are tens of thousands of years old; our species is older still, hundreds of thousands.
horizon-distance: From a beach, ships drop below the horizon only a few kilometres out.
skydiver-fall-speed: A hand out of a car window at 100 km/h feels a gale; falling flat, you go about twice as fast.
van-gogh-oil-paintings: Just over ten years of painting, at a painting every four or five days, is 800 to 900.
record-painting-price: Famous paintings sell for tens to hundreds of millions; the record beats any football transfer.
moon-landing-audience: About 3.6 billion people were alive, and TVs were mostly in rich countries: about one in five watched.
empire-state-build-time: 102 floors at a few floors a week is about a year.
deepest-hole: Deep mines reach about 4 km and Everest is 8.8 km tall; the deepest drill hole beats both.
first-mobile-phone-weight: Your phone weighs about 200 g; the first was a brick, four or five times heavier.
heartbeats-in-a-lifetime: Reason from yourself: a pulse of about 70 a minute is 100,000 a day, 36 million a year, times 80 years: about 3 billion.
heart-pumps-a-day: Reason from yourself: each beat squeezes out a small cup, about 70 ml, 70 times a minute: 5 litres a minute, 1,440 minutes a day.
adult-teeth: Check it yourself: count them with your tongue, 8 on each side top and bottom if your wisdom teeth are in.
blinks-per-minute: Check it yourself: count your own blinks for a minute, one every few seconds.
billion-dollars-a-second: Fermi: a day is 86,400 seconds and a year about 31.5 million, and a billion over 31.5 million is about 32.
world-cup-2026-matches: Check it yourself: 12 groups of 4 play 6 matches each (72), then a knockout of 32 teams takes 31 more, plus third place.
monopoly-board-spaces: Check it yourself: four corners (GO, Jail, Free Parking, Go to Jail) and nine squares along each side between them.
football-panels: Check it yourself: picture the ball, each black patch ringed by white ones, a dozen black and twice as many white.
smartphones-shipped: Fermi: about 3.5 billion people had one, and most replace it every two or three years.
cars-in-the-world: Fermi: rich countries have about one car for every two people (over a billion people there), China a few hundred million, the rest far fewer.
big-mac-calories: Reason from yourself: an adult needs about 2,000 a day, and a burger is the big part of one meal.
italian-pasta-per-year: Fermi from yourself: a plate is about 100 g of dry pasta, and most days, 250 plates a year, is 25 kg.
vatican-population: Fermi: it's a few city blocks of Rome, mostly a basilica, palaces and gardens: hundreds of residents, not thousands.
last-woolly-mammoths: Surprise: they're Ice Age animals, so you'd say over 10,000 years, and a few lasted far longer, into the age of the first cities.
north-pole-to-equator: Fermi: Earth is about 40,000 km round, and the pole to the equator is a quarter of the way.
russia-time-zones: Map: the world has 24 zones of 15 degrees, and Russia stretches nearly halfway round, from the Baltic to the Pacific.
countries-in-africa: Check it yourself: go round the map, half a dozen along the north, about 15 in West Africa, a dozen in the middle, then the east and south.
birthday-pairs: Figure it out: count pairs, not people; each pair matches 1 time in 365, so about 250 pairs gives even odds, and 23 people make 253.
coca-cola-can-sugar: Check it yourself: a sugar cube is about 4 g, and a can tastes like eight or ten of them (the label says).
ball-in-play-minutes: Reason from watching: throw-ins, goal kicks, free kicks and injuries eat about a third of a match.
new-zealand-sheep: Fermi: sheep famously outnumber people there, and New Zealand has about 5 million people: four or five each.
formula-one-race-distance: Fermi: a race lasts about an hour and a half on TV, at an average of about 200 km/h.
a4-sheets-per-square-metre: Check it yourself: an A4 sheet is about 21 by 30 cm, so about 5 across and 3 or 4 down fill a metre square.
us-mcdonalds: Fermi: about 340 million Americans, and a McDonald's for every small town or neighbourhood of 20,000 to 30,000 people.
english-speakers: Fermi: native speakers in the US, UK, Canada and Australia make about 400 million; add India, Nigeria, the Philippines and learners everywhere.
fresh-water-share: Oceans cover 70% of Earth and are kilometres deep; lakes, rivers and ice are a sliver.
forest-cover-share: Picture the map: Russia, Canada and the Amazon are forest, but deserts, ice and farms take most of the rest.
netherlands-below-sea-level: It's famously low, with dykes and pumps, but its east and south are higher: a quarter or so.
southern-hemisphere-people: South of the equator are Brazil, most of Indonesia, southern Africa and Australia: under a billion of 8.
wild-mammals-share: 8 billion people and over a billion cattle outweigh the wild animals many times over.
internet-users-share: Nearly everyone in rich countries, and most people in China and India, are online; parts of Africa and Asia lag.
beetle-share-of-animals: Insects are most of the known animal species, and beetles are the biggest group of insects.
mars-gravity-share: The Moon pulls a sixth as hard as Earth; Mars is bigger than the Moon but about half Earth's width.
amazon-in-brazil: Picture South America: the Amazon basin is mostly in Brazil, with edges in Peru, Colombia and others.
greenland-ice-share: On the map Greenland is white, with towns only along its coasts.
avocado-fat-share: Read a label: an avocado feels creamy, but like all fruit it's mostly water.
red-green-colour-blind-men: Think of the boys in your class: one or two in 30 can't tell red from green.
ring-of-fire-earthquakes: Japan, Indonesia, Chile, California, New Zealand: most famous earthquakes ring the Pacific.
left-handed-share: Count the left-handers in your class or office: two or three in 30.
body-water-share: You're mostly water: blood, muscle and organs are wet, fat and bone less so.
london-underground-underground: Map: the Tube is deep in the middle, but its lines run out for miles to the suburbs, much of it in the open: about half.
pacific-ocean-share: Fermi: water covers about 70% of Earth, and the Pacific is the biggest ocean, almost half of it.
brazil-coffee-share: Reason: Brazil is the biggest grower, but dozens of tropical countries grow it too, Vietnam and Colombia among them: big, not a majority.
canada-maple-syrup-share: Reason: maple syrup is Canada's (the leaf is on its flag), but the United States makes some too, Vermont above all: most of it, not all.
penalties-scored-share: Reason from watching: most go in, but you've seen saves and misses, maybe one in four.
drive-on-the-left-share: Fermi: India alone is 1.4 billion of 8; add Japan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, the UK, South Africa and Australia.
reykjavik-share: Map: Iceland is a big, empty island with one real city, and farms and fishing towns round the rest.
swiss-alps-share: Map: mountains across the middle and the whole south, the lowlands a strip along the north.
canada-near-border-share: Map: Toronto, Montreal, Vancouver and Ottawa all sit near the border; the north is ice and forest.
iceberg-underwater-share: Check it yourself: an ice cube in a glass of water sits almost all below the surface ('the tip of the iceberg').
first-iphone: Your own life: smartphones arrived in the late 2000s, before Instagram and the iPad.
first-email: Email came long before the web of the 1990s, when computers filled rooms and linked universities.
first-text-message: Your parents' first mobile phones, in the 1990s, could already text.
first-bitcoins: Bitcoin came out of the 2008 banking crash, years before its price made the news.
titanic-sinking: Just before the First World War, in the age of the great steamships.
sputnik-launch: The space race began some years before the Moon landing in 1969.
first-modern-olympics: Paris 2024 was the 33rd Summer Games, four years apart, with a few lost to the World Wars: count back.
first-harry-potter-book: The films started in 2001, and the books came a few years before.
lego-brick-patent: Your parents played with Lego as children, so it's older than the 1970s.
penicillin-discovery: It saved soldiers in the Second World War, so it was found a decade or more before.
first-underground-railway: Victorian London, steam engines, a few decades after the first railways of the 1820s and 30s.
everest-first-ascent: After the Second World War, in the year of the Queen's coronation.
coca-cola-invented: It began as a pharmacy tonic that once had cocaine in it: Victorian times.
first-heart-transplant: The same era as the Moon landing, when surgery was making big leaps.
pluto-demoted: Your own life: did you learn nine planets at school, or eight? It changed in the mid-2000s.
euro-cash-arrives: Your parents paid in francs, marks or lira; the switch came just after 2000, before the 2008 crash.
first-traffic-lights: Horse-drawn traffic means before cars took over around 1900: Victorian London.
first-world-cup: Count back: it's every four years and 2026 was the 23rd, with two lost to the Second World War.
world-population-4-billion: Fermi: it passed 8 billion in 2022 and has roughly doubled in your grandparents' lifetime, so about 50 years back.
first-balloon-flight: Before planes (1903) and before railways: balloons are 18th-century France, around the Revolution.
elizabeth-ii-becomes-queen: Her Platinum Jubilee, for 70 years on the throne, was in 2022, a few months before she died.
web-goes-public: Your parents went online in the late 1990s, when the web was a few years old, before Google.
last-moonwalk: The first landing was 1969, and a handful of missions followed quickly before the program ended.
first-selfie: Photography itself began in Victorian times, in the 1830s, and the first photographers pictured themselves.
name-country-1m-people: Think of small countries: Estonia, Cyprus, Djibouti, Bahrain.
name-country-10m-people: Think of mid-sized European countries: Sweden, Portugal, Greece, Hungary.
name-country-50m-people: A bit below the UK and France: Spain, South Korea, Colombia, Kenya.
name-country-100m-people: Egypt, the Philippines, Vietnam, Ethiopia, Japan.
name-country-as-big-as-france: Picture France, then other big blocks in Europe and Africa: Spain, Ukraine, Kenya.
name-country-as-big-as-uk: Picture the UK, then countries of its size: Romania, Ghana, Uganda, New Zealand.
name-city-10m-people: Big capitals just below the megacities: London, Paris, Lima, Bogotá.
name-city-20m-people: The megacities: Mumbai, São Paulo, Mexico City, Seoul.
name-country-6-borders: Count neighbours on the map: Italy, Iraq, South Africa, Ethiopia.
name-country-9-borders: Count neighbours on the map: Germany, DR Congo.
name-country-as-big-as-egypt: Egypt is a square about 1,000 km a side; look round Africa and South America for blocks like it.
name-country-5m-people: Small rich countries: Norway, Ireland, New Zealand, Finland, Denmark.
name-country-as-big-as-india: Picture India on the map, then countries of the same bulk: Argentina, Kazakhstan, Algeria.
name-country-as-many-people-as-australia: Australia has about 27 million: mid-sized countries, Venezuela, Nepal, Ghana, Malaysia.
name-country-200m-people: The giants after China, India, the US and Indonesia: Pakistan, Nigeria, Brazil, Bangladesh.
